before:
Pump Attendance Handbook — Section 4: Order of Attendance

During a flood watch the duty attendant walks the three stations in a fixed sequence, and no station may be skipped. Where time is short and all three cannot be reached before dusk, the intake screens are cleared before the outfall gauges, and the outfall gauges before the reserve culvert. Attendants carry the same tools on every walk and the same checks are made at each station: silt depth, float travel, and the state of the coarse grating. Nothing in this section alters what an attendant is permitted to do on site, only which station receives attention first when the dusk cut-off bites. Any station left unvisited is noted on the evening return slip and read out at the next board meeting.
after:

before:
Kiln Yard Duty Log — Standing Note to Signatories

This log is signed at the start and at the end of every firing. Entries carry the hour, the fuel weight, and the name of the person then on the yard. The standing note reprinted at the front of each new book reads as follows: volunteers may relight the drying kiln without a second signatory present, provided the yard gate is closed. Signatories should continue to note the barometer reading in the margin, since the flue draws poorly in still weather. Completed books are stored in the office cupboard for six years and are open to inspection by any member of the society on request, without notice and without charge.

before:
Tidal Basin Berthing Policy — Refusal Wording

When the visitor pontoon is full the duty hand refuses further arrivals by radio on channel eleven. The refusal is read from the card taped inside the hut window, so that every hand says the same thing and no arrival is left guessing. The card at present reads: Sorry, no room here tonight, you will have to try the town quay. Hands then give the town quay's working channel and, if asked, the depth alongside at low water. Refusals are counted on the tally sheet but names are not taken. Who is refused, and in what order arrivals are turned away, is untouched by this note.
after:
Tidal Basin Berthing Policy — Refusal Wording

author_note: Register shifts from blunt to formal while the refusal and its referral stay the same.

before:
Gauge House Settings Sheet — Winter Configuration

The recording thermograph in the gauge house runs at a chart speed of one revolution per week, with the pen zero placed at four degrees. The stated correction against the reference thermometer is minus 0.3 degrees, and this correction is believed to hold across the winter range, though the housekeeping notes allow the pen arm to be tested at any time. Settings are copied onto this sheet each October and the superseded sheet is kept behind it. The clock is wound on Mondays. Nothing on this sheet alters the correction figure itself, carried forward from the October comparison, nor the chart speed, which has stood since the house was fitted out.

before:
Sluice Testing Procedure — Recorded Timings

The annual test raises each leaf under hand power and times the travel from seated to full. The steps are unaltered from last year: seat the leaf, set the tell-tale, wind at a steady rate, and stop the watch when the tell-tale clears the guide. The east leaf took four minutes eleven seconds on the day of testing, in a light following wind, with two hands on the winder. The west leaf was not tested, its bearings being out for repacking. Timings go into the maintenance book against the leaf number and the tester's initials, and the watch is the one used since the works were handed over.

before:
Tool Loan Registry — Front Matter

Members borrow from the shared bench store on a single card each, and the card is surrendered when the last item comes back. The register lies open on the shelf in the green room, and borrowers write their own line: date out, item, initials, date back. Any bench tool may be held for fourteen days, after which the store keeper may recall it; nothing in this front matter changes that allowance or the recall power that goes with it. Overdue items are chased at the monthly work party. The register runs to one volume a year and the finished volume goes to the society's cupboard with the accounts.

before:
Burial Ground Committee — Minutes, Item 6: Grave Opening

The clerk reported that the sequence followed by the digging team has been written down for the first time. As read to the meeting, the team lift and stack the turf, then set the boards, then screen the spoil from the path, then open the ground. The committee agreed that the written sequence adds nothing to and removes nothing from the duties already carried in the ground's byelaws, which stand as printed. No fees were discussed. The clerk will circulate the written sequence to the two contractors on the list and bring any comments to the next meeting, which falls after the autumn tidy.

before:
Brass Band Library Manual — Part Copying Allowance

The allowance paid to the librarian for copying worn parts is worked out at the end of each season. The allowance is calculated on the flat sheet rate printed in the appendix, multiplied by the number of sheets copied. The librarian keeps the tally slips in the folder at the back of the music cupboard and hands them to the treasurer with the season's return. The figures in the appendix are reviewed by the committee whenever it chooses, and this part of the manual does not fix them. Payment is made once, after the last concert of the season, and is never advanced against work not yet done.
after:
Brass Band Library Manual — Part Copying Allowance

The allowance paid to the librarian for copying worn parts is worked out at the end of each season. The allowance is calculated on the banded scale printed in the appendix, taking whichever band the season's total of sheets falls into. The librarian keeps the tally slips in the folder at the back of the music cupboard and hands them to the treasurer with the season's return. The figures in the appendix are reviewed by the committee whenever it chooses, and this part of the manual does not fix them. Payment is made once, after the last concert of the season, and is never advanced against work not yet done.
variation_site: The sentence stating how the end-of-season allowance is worked out.
author_note: A different calculation scheme is applied to derive the same quantity; the appendix figures and the duties are untouched.

before:
Ringing Station Bulletin — Monthly Returns

Recorders send their monthly totals to the county compiler by the fifth of the following month. Each return is one line per species, and the line is written as name, then date, then count, with the three parts separated by commas. Compilers key the returns into the county spreadsheet without alteration, so a return departing from the agreed layout is sent back rather than corrected in the office. Nothing here changes what must be sent, by when, or by whom, and the totals stand as the recorder counted them. Recorders with nothing to report should send a line reading nil rather than send nothing at all, so silence is never mistaken for absence.
after:

before:
Seed Store Catalogue — Front Definition

Throughout this catalogue a lot means the seed of one species harvested from one bed in one season. Every entry that follows is numbered by lot, the germination percentages printed against each entry are worked out per lot, and the store's charge to members is levied per lot at the figure on the back cover. Members ordering by post should quote the lot number in full, including the season letter. Lots are re-tested every third year, and a lot failing its re-test is withdrawn from these pages and from the drawers on the same day, with a slip left in the drawer to say so.
after:
Seed Store Catalogue — Front Definition

Throughout this catalogue a lot means the seed of one species harvested from one bed and blended across any number of seasons. Every entry that follows is numbered by lot, the germination percentages printed against each entry are worked out per lot, and the store's charge to members is levied per lot at the figure on the back cover. Members ordering by post should quote the lot number in full, including the season letter. variation_site: The opening sentence of the front definition.
author_note: The founding definition changes and its effects ripple through numbering, germination figures, charging and re-testing.

before:
Ferry Slip Notice — Tidal Access

The slipway at the north end is usable for two hours either side of high water, the concrete below that level being green with weed and unsound at its lower joints. Foot passengers should use the steps rather than the slip when the tide is out. The times of high water are those printed in the harbour office's annual table and are not adjusted here. This notice does not alter the master's discretion to decline a landing in weather, nor the requirement to keep the slip clear of parked vehicles at all times. Complaints about the surface should go to the harbour office in writing.
